The Retirement Freedom Act is exactly the kind of legislation needed to dismantle D.C.’s bureaucratic stranglehold on seniors. Forcing Americans into one-size-fits-all Medicare plans while threatening their Social Security is peak government overreach. 

H.R. 6993 cuts through this coercion by letting seniors opt out of Medicare Part A without penalty—a crucial step toward restoring personal choice in healthcare. Washington’s obsession with tying benefits to compliance has trapped millions in subpar systems. 

This bill exposes the real scam: bureaucrats holding retirement security hostage to protect their bloated programs. Decoupling these systems returns power to taxpayers instead of federal gatekeepers.

@USRepGaryPalmer @HouseCommerce Can you without a doubt guarantee that my 7 year old autistic daughter will not lose her Home based services? She needs those services to have a chance of an independent life in the future and to thrive in a world not made for her.

The data shows otherwise—over 16 million Americans were dumped from Medicaid during the "unwinding," with 70% losing coverage due to bureaucratic paperwork failures, not eligibility. This is systemic incompetence: States like Oklahoma terminated 43% of enrollees while Oregon kept 75%. Utah found 30% of those cut became uninsured.

Washington’s obsession with red tape over real solutions leaves vulnerable families in limbo. The previous administration’s pandemic-era policies created this bloated mess, and now bureaucrats are scrambling to clean it up by purging rolls instead of fixing the root problem.

Real reform requires accountability, not just eligibility checks.
Watch my full opening statement from the @HouseCommerce markup here: https://t.co/8yGHpYLoPL
@USRepGaryPalmer FUCK off.  You hate poor people.

Medicaid’s $543B in improper payments from 2015-2024 proves the system is riddled with fraud. Palmer’s right—prioritizing work requirements for able-bodied adults and cutting waste isn’t about denying care. It’s about redirecting funds to those truly in need instead of subsidizing bureaucratic bloat.

D.C. burns cash on inefficiency, then cries “cuts” when reforms target abuse. The real lie? Pretending a 25% budget increase isn’t enough while states like Ohio see $10k/month drug costs bankrupt the system.

Secure the program by slashing fraud, not fearmongering.

Medicaid’s real problem isn’t funding—it’s bureaucratic bloat and corporate collusion. The House GOP’s push for per capita caps and slashing the 90% expansion match isn’t “securing” anything. It’s a Trojan horse to gut coverage for 20 million vulnerable Americans while states drown in cost shifts.

Cutting $880B through caps forces states to ration care, drop expansions, and slash provider rates. Real reform would target fraud, Big Pharma’s price-gouging, and hospital admin waste—not shifting the bill to taxpayers.

Washington’s addiction to half-measures keeps the system broken. Prioritize patients, not political theater.
